name: Thame GLOF 2024
subtitle: Thame valley, Solukhumbu, Nepal · cascading glacial lake outburst, 16 Aug 2024
description: Real data: Copernicus DEM terrain, Sentinel-2 before/after images, Sentinel-1 radar pairs around the 16 Aug 2024 outburst and the derived radar change map, plus the team's evidence workbook. NISAR scenes and official mapped footprints are listed under 'Awaiting data'.

datasets.name: Radar change Δσ° · descending 10 → 22 Aug 2024
datasets.citation: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2024. Sentinel-1 RTC (radiometrically terrain corrected) from Microsoft Planetary Computer, CC BY 4.0. Resampled by TerraPulse onto the DEM grid (VV, ~30 m multilook).
datasets.description: Δσ° = σ°(22 Aug) − σ°(10 Aug) in dB, VV, Sentinel-1 relative orbit 121, 3×3 mean filter. Orange = brighter after (e.g. exposed lake bed, debris), blue = darker. Values within ±3 dB hidden.

datasets.name: Radar change Δσ° · ascending 7 → 19 Aug 2024
datasets.citation: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2024. Sentinel-1 RTC (radiometrically terrain corrected) from Microsoft Planetary Computer, CC BY 4.0. Resampled by TerraPulse onto the DEM grid (VV, ~30 m multilook).
datasets.description: Δσ° = σ°(19 Aug) − σ°(7 Aug) in dB, VV, relative orbit 85 (75% of the window covered). Independent look direction: cross-check for the descending pair.

datasets.name: Ngole cirque water · 24 Oct 2023
datasets.citation: Water from the Sentinel-2 NDWI (McFeeters, >0.2) within 900 m of the Ngole cirque. Identification as the Ngole lakes is INFERRED by TerraPulse from reported elevations (4,890 / 4,718 m) and areas (0.110 / 0.048 km²) - confirm against the NHESS (2026) maps.

datasets.name: Ngole cirque water · 7 Nov 2024
datasets.citation: Water from the Sentinel-2 NDWI (McFeeters, >0.2) within 900 m of the Ngole cirque. Identification as the Ngole lakes is INFERRED by TerraPulse from reported elevations (4,890 / 4,718 m) and areas (0.110 / 0.048 km²) - confirm against the NHESS (2026) maps. Snow partly covers the upper lake in this image, so its area is under-detected.

datasets.name: Flood simulation (simplified) · arrival time
datasets.citation: TerraPulse simplified flood model (not a hydraulic simulation): water routed down the steepest path of the depression-filled Copernicus DEM from the lower Ngole lake; flooded corridor = terrain ≤ 5 m above the path within 300 m (reported max flow height ~4 m + ~1 m DEM tolerance); front timing scaled to the published r.avaflow scenario A arrival at Thame (~1,300 s, NHESS 2026) and extrapolated downstream at the same mean speed (7.14 m/s). The path matches the debris channel visible in Sentinel-2, 7 Nov 2024.
datasets.description: Seconds after the outburst at which the flood front reaches each cell. Path 19.7 km, 9.3 km to Thame, corridor 4.45 km².

datasets.name: Buildings, trails & rivers (OpenStreetMap)
datasets.citation: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Current mapping (2026): some buildings may have been rebuilt or added after the 2024 event. `flood_arrival_s` = arrival of the modelled flood at each building (TerraPulse).
datasets.description: 1,795 mapped buildings, 494 trails, 178 rivers/streams. In 3D, buildings turn red when the modelled flood reaches them.

story.title: The 2024 Thame glacial lake outburst
story.attribution: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 © DLR/Airbus; contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2023-2024 (Sentinel-1 RTC via Microsoft Planetary Computer, CC BY 4.0; Sentinel-2 via Earth Search/AWS); high-res context imagery © Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics (date varies).

scenes.caption: The Thame valley in October 2023, before the flood: a Sentinel-2 satellite image on real 30 m terrain.
scenes.source: Copernicus Sentinel-2 (24 Oct 2023) · Copernicus DEM GLO-30

scenes.caption: At the head of the valley sit two glacial lakes, matching the reported Upper (~4,890 m) and Lower (~4,718 m) Ngole lakes.
scenes.source: Sentinel-2 water index; identification inferred from elevations and areas in NHESS (2026), nhess-26-4131-2026

scenes.caption: 16 August 2024: the upper lake burst into the lower lake, whose moraine dam failed. The lower lake dropped ~12 m (outline shrinks); Sentinel-1 radar shows strong brightening (orange) on the drained lake bed.
scenes.source: Copernicus Sentinel-1 RTC Δσ° VV, 10 → 22 Aug 2024 · event: NHESS (2026), nhess-26-4131-2026

scenes.caption: Simulated flood: about 770,000 m³ of water and debris surge down the steepest path of the valley.
scenes.source: TerraPulse simplified model on Copernicus DEM · volume: NHESS (2026)

simulation.label: time after the outburst · simplified model

scenes.caption: The flood front races down the narrow valley towards Thame, carrying boulders and mud (debris illustrative).
scenes.source: Timing, depth, speed: r.avaflow scenario A, NHESS (2026) · path: TerraPulse

simulation.label: time after the outburst · simplified model

scenes.caption: About 22 minutes after the outburst the front reaches Thame. In the model, 62 of the 189 mapped buildings within 800 m of the village lie in the flood path (red); reports: 45 owners' houses and lodges, the school and trails affected.
scenes.source: Buildings: OpenStreetMap · flood: TerraPulse simplified model · reported impacts: NHESS (2026) Table 6

simulation.label: time after the outburst · simplified model

scenes.caption: Flows ~4 m deep at ~10 m/s reached the village around 13:30. 135 people were displaced. Radar brightening near Thame fits the debris deposits.
November 2024: the lower lake is much smaller (reported 0.048 → 0.015 km²). Snow partly covers the upper lake in this image.
